en: So we had a look at Bun for adding and
managing dependencies, for running code and
for using certain Bun runtime features and
also as a test runner.
Now it's worth noting that you can also
configure the behavior of Bun in a given
project by adding a bunfig.toml file.
Now in that file, you can configure lots of
things and it's also worth pointing out that
you can also store a global bunfig.toml file
in your user's home folder. Or a
project-specific bunfig.toml file as I just
did it.
And as mentioned, you can configure lots of
things in there. Now,
the default settings of course typically are
just fine. You don't need to tweak things
here.
But one setting I, for example, do like to
tweak is related to package management.
Specifically,
I want to
ensure that ignore scripts is set to true,
which is the default, but if that ever
should change, I wanna make sure that it,
well, goes back to
disabled. So I'll set ignore scripts to
true.
And that simply ensures that any scripts
that come attached to dependencies I install
are ignored, are not executed, which as
mentioned earlier, can help you protect
against certain kinds of supply chain
attacks.
In addition, there is the minimum release
age setting here, which I also like to add.
This ensures that whenever I run bun update
or I add a package,
it actually does not install or update to
the very latest version, even if that is a
safe minor or patch release, but instead it
only updates to or installs a package
version that is at least that old. And that
is in seconds. This here is 3 days. So if
there is a supply chain attack, for example,
going on right now and I run bun add, I'll
not be hit because I'm not installing the
malicious version of the package, which
might be live right now.
I only install slightly older versions. And
since supply chain attacks are typically
caught pretty quickly,
only installing versions that are at least 3
days old should be another great layer that
protects me against supply chain attacks. So
that's also something worth knowing about,
which I like to add to my projects.
